name: Eswatini

facts.religion: Christian about 90%, often mixed with traditional belief

snapshot: Africa's last absolute monarchy, where King Mswati III appoints the government and political parties cannot contest elections.
culture: Swazi identity is tied closely to the monarchy and its ceremonies. The Umhlanga reed dance brings tens of thousands of young women to present reeds to the queen mother, and the Incwala is a sacred kingship ritual. siSwati is spoken by nearly everyone. The country changed its name from Swaziland to Eswatini in 2018 by royal decree.
society: The economy is tied to South Africa, which surrounds it on three sides and buys most of its exports, especially sugar and soft-drink concentrate. Eswatini has one of the world's highest HIV rates, though treatment has sharply cut deaths. Pro-democracy protests in 2021 were crushed, with dozens killed.
situation: Mswati III has reigned since 1986. Parliament has elected members but parties are barred from elections, and the king appoints the prime minister and cabinet. Since 2025 Eswatini has accepted people deported from the United States who are not its citizens; a fourth group arrived in July 2026, and local lawyers have challenged the arrangement in court.
power: An absolute monarchy. The king appoints the prime minister, the cabinet and part of parliament and can veto laws; candidates stand as individuals under the tinkhundla system, with political parties excluded.

sources.label: Africanews: fourth group of US deportees
